_readme: A SNAPSHOT of every permission key that has already been released.
It exists because permissions are a stored SNAPSHOT on each role, not a live
reference to permissions.json. The seed writes the whole catalog into the
Administrator role, but with onConflictDoNothing — deliberately, so a boot
cannot re-widen a role an operator narrowed on purpose. The cost is that an
EXISTING role is frozen at whatever the catalog held the day it was created.
So a key added here reaches nobody on an existing database. The symptom is a
403 on a screen the full-access account plainly ought to reach, and it
compounds: assertGrantable refuses to hand out a key the granter does not
hold, so nobody on that role can grant it onward either and the gap cannot be
That has now been repaired by hand FOUR times - migrations 0068, 0075, 0085
and 0087 - and every one of them was found by a person hitting the wall in a
permission-catalog-baseline.spec.ts fails when permissions.json and this file
disagree. Adding a key is therefore two deliberate steps: write the migration
that grants it to the roles that should have it, then add the key here. The
second step is what says 'I have thought about the existing databases'.
